rationale: ⚠️ The singular user routes consistently group activation with other individual-user operations. The plural activation path appears to be a documentation typo.
⚠️ JSON filters are the input; event-stream formats are negotiated output. The contract incorrectly repeats response stream media types under consumes.
⚠️ Exhausted optimistic-concurrency retries deliberately produce conflict. The deletion response list omits this legitimate 409 outcome.
⚠️ URL parsing fails before permission verification, but Error only writes JSON and leaves the success status. A verification failure must not appear successful.
⚠️ The invoice error branch lacks a return. Both response helpers serialize a body, so the handler writes an error followed by success instead of one JSON response.
⚠️ Renamed DTO properties have explicit model-to-DTO mappings only. Creation uses the unmapped reverse direction, losing documented client name, homepage and redirect URLs.
⚠️ The configurable message limit and explicit validation appear intentional. The request schema omits that operational constraint and its default.
⚠️ Verification checks references only in the supplied context, while deletion selects solely by asset ID. Ownership is never established, allowing deletion outside the authorized context.
⚠️ Deletion is explicitly filter driven. Its parameter annotation names deleteRelationTuple, while the operation uses deleteRelationTuples; the generated contract consequently omits query filters.
⚠️ Missing-image errors are translated to resource-not-found, then indiscriminately returned as 500. The handler should preserve the documented missing-resource outcome.
⚠️ Administrative language options are intentionally behind administrator authentication. The contract lacks the security requirement enforced by the route group.
⚠️ Unknown flags deliberately return a blank evaluation with a diagnostic and zero flagID. The response schema excludes this explicit fallback representation.
⚠️ Omission intentionally selects the configured global depth, as the engine comment explains. Marking max-depth required misstates this supported default.
⚠️ The handler counts suppressed findings but removes them from the body. The total header therefore does not count the returned finding population.

⚠️ Namespace switches intentionally control both UI visibility and evaluation participation. The contract describes all stored flag enrichers, overstating the enabled effective catalog returned by this mapper.
⚠️ Glob is explicitly enabled and has its own storage schema alongside exact and regex. The flavor documentation is incomplete.
⚠️ Multipart BOM upload dispatches a scan event into the dependency-check parser. The JSON BOM path uses BomUploadEvent, corroborating a mistaken event dispatch in the multipart path.
⚠️ The batch handler iterates flag IDs exclusively. Documented flagKeys are ignored, so a valid key-only batch returns no evaluations.
⚠️ Input conversion preserves PurgeOnDelete, but output conversion copies only three cleanup fields. The missing assignment silently changes true to false in returned configurations.
⚠️ The early issuer-error branch uses the plain status helper instead of the introspection error writer used nearby, violating the documented JSON error format.
⚠️ This operation constructs cluster connectivity and node counts in a clusterSummary envelope. The controller-status response annotation describes a different operation.
⚠️ The operation reads available command types without modifying state. GET matches that purpose; the contract incorrectly declares POST.
⚠️ The handler deliberately returns a blank result and diagnostic when lookup fails. The positive-only flagID schema omits the zero sentinel used for that fallback.
⚠️ The organization-key collection and member routes consistently use singular org. The plural orgs segment in the member contract is inconsistent with that route family.
⚠️ Routing intentionally separates the collection from wildcard file retrieval. The documented trailing slash selects the file route instead of the listing route.
⚠️ Tag deletion is deliberately registered among authenticated mutations. Its contract omits the authentication requirement enforced by that group.
⚠️ Both endpoint documentation and parameter annotations require namespace. The read handler never validates its presence, allowing the generic persistence query to span namespaces.
⚠️ The template and handler agree on hash. Declaring thumb leaves the actual required path variable undefined, exposing an internally inconsistent contract.
⚠️ UpdateProcess reports an unknown ID, but the handler maps every update error to 400. It fails to distinguish the documented missing-process case.
⚠️ The shared request layer intentionally returns 400 for undecodable parameters before dispatch. The endpoint response list omits this malformed-request outcome.
⚠️ Reading interface settings needs no comment payload. AddCommentReq is an unrelated copied body annotation; the handler correctly just retrieves configuration.
⚠️ The read mapper intentionally lists namespaces whose environment switch permits execution. The contract fails to qualify flag-scoped enrichers as enabled and overstates the effective catalog.
⚠️ The resource forwards an omitted parent as null, and persistence explicitly clears the relationship. That contradicts the operation's explicit promise to preserve the existing parent.
⚠️ A references endpoint appropriately returns referencing components. The annotation mistakenly describes a controller service rather than the references envelope.
⚠️ Search accepts a result count and offset and returns matching labels. A single-object response annotation is incompatible with this collection operation.
⚠️ Successful POST login returns the user without storing USER_ID_KEY. GET authentication and logout explicitly use that session attribute, confirming the missing session establishment.
⚠️ The contract prose itself says only namespace is required. Optional object and relation filters match that intent; their required flags contradict it.
⚠️ Filtering accumulates into a nil Policies slice. With no matches, the nil result reaches the JSON writer; initializing an empty slice would preserve the promised array shape.
⚠️ The users collection retrieves User records. Referencing Position in its response schema is an unrelated model substitution in the contract.
⚠️ Constraint deletion uses only constraintID; segmentID is unused and flagID selects snapshot history. The transaction helper adds no membership check, so nested resource ownership is unenforced.
⚠️ The output cleanup mapper omits PurgeOnDelete even though input mapping preserves it. A stored true value therefore becomes false in the returned process configuration.
⚠️ Segment deletion selects solely by segmentID. flagID is used for snapshot and notification bookkeeping, without validating that the deleted segment belongs to that flag.
⚠️ The DAO takes no pagination arguments and the manager wraps the entire result without slicing. The resource consequently ignores the page-selection contract.
⚠️ The implementation intentionally defines and returns an apiAllKeys envelope containing keys. The bare-array contract omits that explicit response wrapper.

⚠️ The supplied authorization callback checks the updated context, affected components and service references, but never authorizes reads on inherited contexts. The documented inheritance permission requirement is unenforced in this path.
⚠️ HEAD uses the verification handler whose malformed-URL branch writes an error without changing status. The response can signal success despite verification never completing.
⚠️ The router reserves the exact slashless collection path for listing and the slash wildcard for file retrieval. The listing annotation includes an erroneous trailing slash.
⚠️ The handler puts false into a boolean struct field, and GORM excludes blank fields from predicates. Explicit enabled=false therefore loses its filter and can return enabled flags.
⚠️ sitemap.html resolves an HTML template through the configured HTML view resolver. The text/plain produces declaration misdescribes the intended HTML representation.
⚠️ Organization-key operations share the singular org route family in the router. The plural member path in the contract is a documentation inconsistency.
⚠️ PATCH updates the DTO then invokes toModel, whose renamed properties lack reverse mappings. Submitted name, homepage and redirect URL changes do not reach their model properties.
⚠️ Position exposes a structured Network bean with named properties. The response schema's string type fails to describe that model.
⚠️ Streaming chat deliberately enforces a configurable message-length limit, defaulting to 4000. The shared message schema omits this constraint.
⚠️ The concrete route and handler both remove one path-identified member. The collection-path annotation and plural body schema appear stale; the summary also describes removing a single member.
⚠️ The suggestion writer deliberately uses the API's query_time, record_count and page_size naming and emits item tags as labels. The contract describes a different naming scheme.
⚠️ The role filter initializes a nil result slice and only appends matches. Empty results therefore reach the JSON writer as null instead of the documented array.
⚠️ Route reports return Position beans whose network property is a structured Network object. The contract incorrectly types this property as a string.
⚠️ The endpoint explicitly returns all album share links, and Links is a slice. The single-Link response annotation incorrectly models this collection.
⚠️ An absent image becomes ErrResourceNotFound in persistence, but the details handler converts it to a typed 500 response. This loses the documented 404 distinction.
⚠️ Glob has explicit enabled-flavor and storage support, and deletion accepts any enabled flavor. The contract's two-flavor description is incomplete.
⚠️ Deleting a listing request returns its listing status and envelope, matching the operation's purpose. DropRequestEntity is a copied annotation for a different queue operation.
